statement: When an initialized hosted partition loses its raft-rs host during an existing-origin participant release, the registered participant release recovery owner retains one bounded continuation while the canonical port status says the group is held by host recovery. The existing raft-rs runtime owner reconstructs and replays the group; only a later fresh observation of an actual current leader may enter the unchanged current origin, build, membership, generation, drain, census and resume release path. A healthy follower remains event-driven, recovery stays single-flight and bounded, and replacement or shutdown cannot reopen stale service admission.

constraints.statement: Reuse the raft-rs runtime's existing reconstruction path, the write kernel's canonical held-status classifier, the release recovery owner's existing pending/running/timer state and the canonical participant cutover. Add no second release algorithm, timer, election driver, ledger or status interpretation.

A retained wake carries no release permission. Reopening still requires a freshly observed current leader and the unchanged durable origin, measured build, live service identity, membership, generation, drain, query settlement and exact census checks.

The sealed red must use the real registered ReplicaHandler and raft-rs owners. It may passively observe owner events and actual-core reconstruction, but must not manually call readStatus after healing, sleep for a typed retry, tick the core, repeat operator release, alter pause state or otherwise supply the missing actuation.

Keep the existing healthy 10000 ms group bound and production retry/cutover budgets. A fully spent healthy bound is red. Validate any port-provided retry duration and schedule it on the release owner's existing clock without a tight loop or deadline conversion across clocks.

Only the canonical typed host-held outcome retains recovery debt. An ordinary follower, candidate, absent service, invalid status or service with no current identity remains event-driven and cannot become a polling release authority.
Preserve per-partition single-flight, the global concurrency limit, event coalescing, current-service revalidation after await, service replacement safety and shutdown cancellation/settlement.

Do not absorb TX1 deletion, M1 provisioning, W1 unknown-phase recovery, C2 rebalancer cleanup, FreshMG activation, snapshot custody or unrelated startup policy. Source changes require category-complete independent design and implementation review plus exact locked-lab source-revert proof.
